controlName: Appropriate Methods and Metrics Are Identified and Applied
purpose: Ensures the right metrics are chosen to actually measure the risks that matter for a given AI system, rather than defaulting to generic or convenient measurements.
summary: Appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied, matched to the system's context and socio-technical impacts, regularly reassessed for continued validity, and applied by internal experts or independent assessors who weren't the system's front-line developers.
expectedStatementElements: How metrics were selected to match the system's specific risk context, not just generic performance metrics
How often metrics are reassessed for continued appropriateness and validity
Whether evaluations are conducted by people independent of the system's original development
What socio-technical (not just technical) factors the chosen metrics account for
evidenceExamples: Metric selection rationale tied to the system's specific risk context
Metric review schedule and revision history
Documentation showing evaluators were independent of front-line development
Socio-technical impact considerations built into the measurement approach
commonGaps: Only generic accuracy metrics are tracked, missing context-specific risks
Metrics were chosen once at launch and never reassessed
The same developers who built the system are the only ones evaluating it
Measurement focuses purely on technical performance with no socio-technical dimension
interviewQuestions: How did you decide which metrics actually matter for this system's specific risks?
When was the last time you reassessed whether your metrics are still the right ones?
Who evaluates this system — is it independent from the people who built it?
Do your metrics capture anything beyond raw technical performance?
